display.title: The Secret of the Name of Hashem, Part 2
display.summary_short: The Arab sheikh reveals his secret to Rabbi Moshe Galanti: deep reverence for Hashem's holy name. Then a parable and a true story about the power of a child's tefillah.
display.summary_long: After a recap, Rabbi Moshe Galanti completes his two-day fast and returns to the sheikh, who leads him through a locked room, a garden pool where they immerse, and into a splendid house with a jeweled Aron Kodesh. Afraid of bowing to something improper, Rabbi Moshe bows with the words "I place Hashem before me". Inside the ark he finds a plaque with a menorah and the verse Shivisi, the four letters of Hashem's name written large. The sheikh explains that when he prays for the sick, he looks at the name: if it shines, the person will live. Rabbi Moshe goes home both happy and in tears, realizing how much more honor he owes Hashem's name, and he tells the story so that everyone will think of Hashem's greatness before saying His name. The storyteller adds that we should say brachos and davening clearly, gives a parable of a wise man who asked a king for permission to visit him every day, and tells of a doctor whose adopted five-year-old son davened from a homemade siddur for a baby brother, and that year his prayer was answered.
display.lesson: Say Hashem's name and every word of brachos and davening clearly and with awe, because Hashem listens to every tefillah.

sources_cited.note: Shivisi Hashem l'negdi samid, written on the plaque.

segments.title: The secret behind the silver doors
segments.summary: The sheikh shows Rabbi Moshe the holy name in his ark and explains how he knows whether the sick will recover.

segments.title: Saying brachos clearly
segments.summary: We speak to Hashem clearly and respectfully, as we would to a person.

segments.title: Parable: the king's daily visitor
segments.summary: A wise man asks the king for permission to visit him every day, like our invitation to daven.

segments.title: The doctor and the homemade siddur
segments.summary: A boy's prayer from his own siddur for a baby brother is answered.

identity_guesses.evidence_quote: I believe in Hashem. I trust in Hashem.
